name: Soldering

claims.claim_text: The technique taught to a beginner reduces to holding the tip flat against the joint so it makes contact, letting heat transfer, and then feeding solder in.
claims.quote_verbatim: the tip had to be flat and on there so it makes contact and then you just feed the solder in
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The characteristic beginner error is attempting every part of the operation at once — holding the component, the board, the iron and the solder simultaneously — when the work should be arranged so that everything is already in position and the joint simply held long enough for heat to transfer.
claims.quote_verbatim: they try and hold the component and hold the PCB and hold the soldering and hold the, hold the solder
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Teaching is more effective when limited to safety and a single minute of demonstration before the learner starts, with technique refined over subsequent projects rather than delivered as a half-hour lesson up front.
claims.quote_verbatim: I wanted him to just do it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The quality of the iron is itself a factor in a beginner's results, since most people start with the cheapest available tool while the technique is being judged.
claims.quote_verbatim: most people, when they start, it's like, you know, Radio Shack, Firebrand, you know, like that kind of thing is not as good
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Poor equipment degrades joint quality measurably, and moving to cartridge-tip irons that can be swapped from a stand as the work requires is described as a substantial step up from low-cost stations.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was starting to affect some of my, my solder joints
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The value of flux is one of the slowest lessons to arrive unaided, and its absence produces joints that fail intermittently rather than obviously — a joint that breaks later or performance that drifts.
claims.quote_verbatim: it took me a long time to learn the value of flux in soldering
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mars, System Design & NAND - Mercurial Mars Mission

claims.claim_text: Solder mask is what makes solder go where it is intended: with flux applied, the solder flows and settles onto the exposed pads rather than spreading, which is a substantial part of what the extra fabrication cost buys.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can just throw some flux on there and the solder flows so nice and it just gets where it's supposed to
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Leaded solder flows more easily than lead-free and produces a better-looking joint; lead-free works but demands more care, and keeping leaded solder available tends to prevent the transition being made at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: It works, you know? It just doesn't look as good. You have to take a bit more care
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SolidCon and Traveling Tech - Joined Junk Jocularity

claims.claim_text: Drag soldering is the technique that marks the boundary of a beginner's course, sitting just beyond through-hole work and short of preheaters and area-array packages.
claims.quote_verbatim: it might finish off with drag soldering SMD, for example, that, that might be as advanced as it would get
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Prior Art, Wafer Fabs and Guns - Whimsical Wafer Waffling

claims.claim_text: Surface-mount work is a distinct skill rather than a harder version of the same one, requiring a steady hand, tweezers and usually a microscope, but is achievable at an ordinary workbench once learned.
claims.quote_verbatim: It does require steady hand and a pair of tweezers and probably a microscope
claims.speaker: Keith Burzinski
claims.episode_title: Automating the Home with Keith Burzinski

claims.claim_text: Header footprints with deliberately staggered pins hold the part in the board by friction so it does not fall out while being soldered.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you stick the headers into the board, they don't fall out whenever you try to solder them
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer and Jeremy Blum - Audacious Arduino Arguments

claims.claim_text: Removing a multi-pin connector is easier if the plastic body is destroyed first so that each pin can then be desoldered individually, which preserves the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: knock, knock the plastic part off, go and then, you know, solder, desolder all the pins
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Modules are attached to a host board through castellations — plated half-holes routed along the board edge — which allows the module to be machine-placed and soldered like any other component.
claims.quote_verbatim: little, you know, half-moon-plated holes on the edge of your board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Speed and joint quality trade against each other directly, a lesson typically learned by soldering as fast as possible and then having to rework the result.
claims.quote_verbatim: I discovered there was a tradeoff between speed and quality
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: A hand-soldered board does not match a reflowed one on appearance, though careful work under a microscope with sufficient time can approach it.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's nothing beats a nice reflowed board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Adequate light is a prerequisite rather than a refinement: roughly a thousand lux at the bench is the working minimum, and joints that appear sound from one angle frequently prove otherwise when the board is picked up and viewed from another.
claims.quote_verbatim: You need at least like a thousand lux.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SolidCon and Traveling Tech - Joined Junk Jocularity

claims.claim_text: A microscope with integral illumination and stereo optics reveals defects that are missed at the bench even with good light and good eyesight.
claims.quote_verbatim: you take it over to the microscope and, you know, hey, there it is
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SolidCon and Traveling Tech - Joined Junk Jocularity

claims.claim_text: The property that makes an optical microscope suitable for soldering rather than only inspection is working distance, since the iron has to fit between the objective and the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: being able to get a soldering iron underneath it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Micro-soldering is supported by dedicated equipment rather than general-purpose tools, with a fine-tipped iron and a microscope treated as the pair required to begin.
claims.quote_verbatim: I got a new micro soldering iron
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching with Michael Ossmann and Dmitry Nedospazov

claims.claim_text: As devices shrink, the response available to a repair practitioner is better magnification and finer tips rather than an objection to the trend, and reballing a three-hundred-ball part is treated as difficult but legitimate work.
claims.quote_verbatim: If stuff gets smaller, I'll just get a better microscope. I mean, I'll get smaller soldering tips.
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: Right To Repair with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: The standards body governing assembly publishes land pattern specifications that fix pad geometry for surface-mount parts, on the basis that pad sizing is what determines whether a joint solders reliably in volume.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's for surface mount components and manufacturing.
claims.speaker: Natasha Baker
claims.episode_title: Footprints and Symbols with Natasha Baker

claims.claim_text: Formal soldering training exists and is oriented to military and long-life assembly, so only a fraction of it transfers to hobbyist work; a week-long specialist course yielded roughly one useful day when filtered for that audience.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe one out of the five days was worthwhile
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: The scope of soldering as a technical subject is far larger than its apparent simplicity suggests, extending to long-term reliability chemistry worth funding a year of research when a product is made in millions.
claims.quote_verbatim: the field of soldering is almost infinite in its scope
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: Claims about exotic solder alloys improving conductivity misplace the effect, since the solder accounts for a negligible fraction of the resistance of a complete connection.
claims.quote_verbatim: the solder is like 0.1% of your whole connection
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: Soldering is not the most reliable joining method available: telecommunications practice favours crimping and wire wrapping, and building wiring standards prohibit soldered connections in favour of screwed and clamped ones.
claims.quote_verbatim: Everything should be crimped or wire wrapped.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: The prohibition is a standards requirement rather than a preference, on the grounds that a soldered joint is not reliable enough for permanently installed wiring.
claims.quote_verbatim: Soldering is totally forbidden, you know, because it isn't reliable enough.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: A connector is more reliable than a hand-soldered joint for anything that will be connected and disconnected repeatedly, which is why test fixtures use pluggable interfaces rather than soldered wiring.
claims.quote_verbatim: connectors more reliable than my soldering
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Where a wire must be soldered directly, the practice is to solder it once, secure it with adhesive and never disturb it again, keeping any connection that needs to be broken on a mating connector instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: I want to solder it once and then, you know, put hot snot all over it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Manufacturers eliminate connectors to save cents at volume, soldering mains and output wiring directly to the board even where the enclosure retains the openings for the screw terminals that were designed out.
claims.quote_verbatim: they solder the wires directly onto the board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Processes that consume a variable liquid or paste — soldering among them — are the hardest to hold consistent in volume manufacturing, and are correspondingly the hardest to anticipate problems in.
claims.quote_verbatim: wet processes, the ones that require consumables, like, uh, soldering are the ones that tend to be really hard
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Machine-applied paste is far more consistent than wire solder fed to a tip, so hand and semi-automated soldering operations vary more than reflow does.
claims.quote_verbatim: SMT is pretty darn close. They're really good at keeping that consistent, but wire solder isn't as close
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consistency in a manual operation is engineered through fixtures that make the correct action easier to perform than the incorrect one, rather than through instruction alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: you make fixtures, you make it so that people have an easier time sticking on a label or doing a solder process and you're going to get more consistent results
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The effective way to get an assembly defect corrected is to document it with evidence rather than describe it: a high-resolution photograph of a tombstoned component typically produces a fix within the hour, where a general complaint does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: a high res photo of a tombstone component is like gold
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Identifying and documenting the problem precisely is the larger share of the work with a remote factory, which is generally both responsive and capable once it knows exactly what is wrong.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not enough to say this feels kind of weird.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Soldering onto unconventional substrates is limited by temperature: printed conductive traces on paper or fabric and their substrate must survive several hundred degrees for the seconds a joint takes, which pushes such work toward low-temperature alloys, very fast technique, or welding instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: your material, your substrate has to take it, your actual traces have to take it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Printed conductive traces on flexible substrates are high-impedance compared with copper — on the order of ohms per inch — which restricts them to low-current sensor and battery wiring.
claims.quote_verbatim: these are higher impedance traces
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: In practice conductive traces printed on microfibre have been soldered with small-outline packages and reflowed successfully, with leaded solder performing better than lead-free, and reflow onto paper also demonstrated.
claims.quote_verbatim: Reflow works really well. And you can use normal lead or lead-free solder.
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner
claims.episode_title: An interview with Ariel Briner of Cartesian Co

claims.claim_text: Substrate resolution rather than the soldering sets the limit on what can be attached: a package cannot be placed on ordinary cotton because the printed resolution is inadequate, whereas microfibre supports it.
claims.quote_verbatim: to print on a regular cotton t-shirt, you couldn't get the resolution
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner
claims.episode_title: An interview with Ariel Briner of Cartesian Co

claims.claim_text: Conductive adhesive dispensed in place of solder paste is an alternative attachment method that removes the temperature constraint entirely.
claims.quote_verbatim: it actually does adhesive, conductive adhesive
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Soldering to a component whose lead has been cut flush with its body remains possible by clearing material around the pin with a rotary tool and attaching a wire to what remains.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can just go around the pin and you can still solder a little wire onto the pin
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Radiation Chips & Old Package Types - Technocratic Toilet Troubleshooting

claims.claim_text: Prefabricated connector pigtails — a connector on one end and stripped tinned wire on the other — remove the need to crimp, since two of them soldered together with heat-shrink produce an adapter between any two connector families.
claims.quote_verbatim: I do not have to crimp wires anymore
claims.speaker: Zach Hoeken
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Hoeken Smith - Creative China Commorant

claims.claim_text: Soldering faults are a favoured explanation during debugging and frequently the wrong one: a board that produced no response was assumed for days to have a soldering problem, and the part was replaced twice, before the actual cause proved to be a reset line held active.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was convinced it was a soldering issue because I had so much trouble with the soldering
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Tesla, Checklists and Bullies - Emerging External Eupsychics

claims.claim_text: Experience can work against the diagnosis, because an experienced engineer generates many plausible hypotheses and pursues them, where an inexperienced one might simply check every pin and find it immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes you can be too clever for your own good, too experienced for your own good
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Tesla, Checklists and Bullies - Emerging External Eupsychics

claims.claim_text: The reverse error is equally common: a week of elaborate protocol workarounds was built to cope with noise on a bus that turned out to be caused by the soldering, and the workarounds proved entirely unnecessary once the joint was fixed.
claims.quote_verbatim: there was noise on the I squared C lines because of my soldering job and everything worked great
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Building Firmware and Hardware for Trade Shows with Mike Szczys

claims.claim_text: Wires soldered on to reach a debug header or serial pins become their own source of doubt, since a broken lead leaves the engineer unsure whether the code or the wiring is being debugged.
claims.quote_verbatim: am I debugging, you know, my code or am I debugging my bad tottering job?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: Skill should be built on work where failure costs nothing rather than on a board that must function: running a bodge wire out from under an area-array package is a high-risk operation to attempt for the first time under deadline.
claims.quote_verbatim: try to practice soldering with low risk projects
claims.speaker: Greg Davill

claims.claim_text: The skill degrades without regular use and improves sharply with daily repetition, which is why technicians who solder every day are markedly better at it than engineers who solder occasionally.
claims.quote_verbatim: the text you get texts are so good because they're doing it every day
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Deliberate practice on a board designed for repetition, aiming at the same joint made well over and over, is more effective than attempting real work and being disappointed by the result.
claims.quote_verbatim: people that want to learn how to solder they sometimes go out and buy like solder practice boards
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: One published practice board arranges the same simple circuit five times in descending package sizes, from through-hole down through progressively smaller outlines and passives, so a single design exercises the full range of hand-assembly difficulty.
claims.quote_verbatim: You made it with dip. You made it with, like, SOIC.
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: Scrap mobile telephone logic boards bought cheaply are used as micro-soldering practice material, since they carry dense runs of the smallest passive sizes.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are used for soldering practice, um, for the cell phone repair folks
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: Advanced hand-assembly techniques are learnable by persistence rather than talent: one practitioner had never worked with flexible boards, area-array packages or much surface mount before doing so on camera, and found it demanding but achievable with the right tools and refined technique.
claims.quote_verbatim: you got to kind of work at it and you got to find the right tools and you got to refine your techniques
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: Soldering produces fumes and requires extraction, which rules it out of ordinary commercial office space along with reflow ovens and chemical etching.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can't even use my reflow oven here in the office right because the smell is just too bad
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Guns and Mobile Labs - Nuanced Nomadic Non-essentials

claims.claim_text: A workshop space intended for hands-on assembly has to be provisioned deliberately with ventilation, good table lighting and long enough working sessions, rather than being an ordinary room with tables.
claims.quote_verbatim: where we could solder, where we could make a mess and have good ventilation and really good table lighting
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Fabienne Serrière of KnitYak

claims.claim_text: Transferring a working breadboard circuit onto soldered perforated board is a productive exercise precisely because mistakes are likely and are cheap to correct with solder and wire, which is where the troubleshooting is learned.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're not going to do it right. You're going to make mistakes and when you make mistakes, that's when you're really, that's when you're teaching yourself
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Perforated board construction remains viable for demanding circuits including radio-frequency work, where the requirements are avoiding excess coupling and checking carefully that nothing is bridged.
claims.quote_verbatim: With RF, you have to be careful a bit that you don't bring too much interference into the circuit.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Careful visual checking under magnification that every joint is isolated from its neighbours is the discipline that makes hand-built board construction reliable.
claims.quote_verbatim: she had a magnification glass and she just looked super carefully that everything was isolated from each other
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Attaching a fine-pitch part to a board whose footprints differ from the reference design turns a routine operation into a problem of locating the correct pads, which is where the instructive difficulty lies.
claims.quote_verbatim: trying to find those pads was, was significantly tricky
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The failure mode that recurs among people new to modular boards is not soldering at all: stacking a shield onto headers without soldering them produces a board that appears connected and does nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to solder the headers to the shield
claims.speaker: Simone Giertz

claims.claim_text: Kit vendors receive returns for exactly that error, which indicates it is a gap in the mental model rather than carelessness on the part of individuals.
claims.quote_verbatim: they get returned kits for the same thing
claims.speaker: Simone Giertz

claims.claim_text: A kit built with poor joints and then returned as defective is a recognised pattern, and one where the assembly rather than the design is the cause is usually evident from photographs of the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's obvious why it didn't work. Oh, my God. Just look at the pictures.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Repair work at the fine end is constrained less by soldering skill than by parts availability, since a replacement controller that differs only in how it communicates may be unobtainable at any price because the manufacturer will not sell it.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no place where I can buy it because the manufacturer says, sorry, we can't sell to you
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: Right To Repair with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: Terminating a high pin count connector by hand is measured in hours per connector, which is why such work is avoided where a terminated assembly can be bought instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: it'd take you an hour or two hours to terminate one of these connectors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Soldering under a camera while narrating is substantially harder than soldering alone, so recorded technique is a poor guide to a practitioner's actual ability.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just so hard under the camera
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Leaded packages can be improvised from a surface-mount board by soldering stamped metal legs to its edge, producing the footprint of a through-hole part.
claims.quote_verbatim: he would solder those to the side of a PCB
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A part supplied only in a leadless package has to be adapted to a breadboard-compatible carrier before it can be used in exploratory work.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I want to use this on a breadboard, I got to dipify it
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

attribution_notes: Episodes on the speaker-map unreliable list are attributed by content or left unattributed.
